complexity.correctness_reason: Once the 100 cap is lifted, m+n greater than about 1000 exceeds CPython's default recursion limit and raises RecursionError (e.g. m = 600, n = 600).
complexity.notes: Correct but exponential. ||Caching the subproblem results (or a bottom-up DP table)|| brings this to O(m*n) time, and ||the combinatorial closed form C(m+n-2, m-1)|| computes it in O(min(m,n)) unit-cost arithmetic. Also note CPython's default recursion limit (~1000) is only safe here because of the m,n <= 100 cap.
complexity.summary: Plain recursion: uniquePaths(m,n) = uniquePaths(m-1,n) + uniquePaths(m,n-1) with base case 1 when either dimension is 1. With no memoization, overlapping subproblems are recomputed exponentially many times; stack depth is O(m+n).
